subject: Peering latency exclusion request — Veridian private deployment
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@veridian.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@veridian.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: peering latency exclusion for Veridian private deployment

Hi Neha,

We're preparing to go live on Redwood Private next month and have a unique network topology at three of our hospitals where the transit hops are customer-managed. Our SREs are seeing a tail in p95-p99 when traffic goes over the customer WAN peering during peak backup windows. We need to request a limited SLA carveout for latency attribution tied specifically to customer-controlled peering and transit.

What we'd like: a documented appendix that excludes latency attributable to our peering/edge in defined conditions (scheduled backups, known WAN maintenance, and an agreed jitter threshold). We can share perf samples and NetFlow for the last 90 days — attached is a CSV with a sample window.

Questions from our side:
- What telemetry signal does Redwood need to validate 'peering-attributable' incidents?
- Can we get a temporary SLA buffer while we implement BGP community tagging and route-level telemetry?

Attaching: peering-latency-metrics.csv (sample), network-diagram.png

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, Veridian Health

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@veridian.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: peering latency exclusion for Veridian private deployment

Hi Samir — thanks for the detailed note and the data. I reviewed the CSV and the topology image; that helps a lot.

High-level response and next steps:
1) We can draft a time-boxed SLA appendix that scopes exclusions to customer-controlled peering where the measured RTT at our ingress exceeds the agreed jitter/latency threshold and other conditions (scheduled backups, documented maintenance windows).
2) For validation we need two telemetry sources: (a) packet-level or flow samples (NetFlow/sFlow) showing the tail coincident with your backup windows, and (b) a route-level tag or BGP community that marks traffic as customer-peered. If BGP tagging is not immediately feasible, we can accept correlated Cloud Router metrics + your runbook entry for the windows as interim evidence.
3) We'll propose a 90-day 'temporary buffer' where Redwood will apply leniency for p95-p99 breaches tied to verified peering incidents; after that buffer both sides implement tagging and continuous telemetry.

I'm looping in Karthik to confirm operational controls and Vanessa for legal/contract redline. I've attached a very rough draft appendix (proposed-sla-appendix-draft.pdf) for discussion — this is intentionally conservative.

Can you confirm: which three sites are in scope, and whether you can enable community tagging within 60 days?

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Commercial Lead, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@veridian.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: peering latency exclusion for Veridian private deployment

Thanks both — quick operational notes from my side.

- Telemetry: For credible attribution we'll accept either (1) BGP community tagging (preferred) plus sampled packet captures at our edge, or (2) if tagging is delayed, then dual-sided NetFlow samples and a signed runbook entry that enumerates the scheduled windows. The appendix should require Veridian to produce the correlated evidence set within 48 hours of an incident to qualify for exclusion.
- Fallback: If evidence is ambiguous, default attribution remains 'customer-side' for latency, but we'll offer a one-time service credit during the 90-day buffer for first confirmed incident while tagging is implemented.
- Monitoring: We will expose a per-tenant 'peering flag' in Console metadata once tagging is enabled so incident buckets are visible to your SREs and ours.

Vanessa — from legal: please start a short-form amendment that references the existing SLA, carves out the narrow set of conditions above, and includes the 90-day buffer and evidence submission timelines. Samir — if you can provide the exact site IDs (Edge-ID-*) and the NetFlow export format we'll validate ingestion paths.

Onboarding checklist for Veridian to close the buffer:
- Enable BGP community tagging at the three peering routers (ETA 60d)
- Share NetFlow schema and a 90-day historical export (done)
- Agree on incident evidence SLA (48h)

-Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@veridian.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Legal Ops <legal@veridian.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Apr 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: peering latency exclusion for Veridian private deployment

Neha, Karthik — appreciate the quick turnaround and the draft appendix. Veridian agrees to the 90-day buffer and the evidence requirements you outlined. Site IDs are: Edge-ID-17, Edge-ID-18, Edge-ID-23. Our network team confirms they can enable community tagging within 45 days (earlier than requested).

Next steps from our side:
- I'll upload full NetFlow exports for the last 90 days to the HubSpot secure file link (expect by Tue).
- Legal will redline the appendix; I've sent Legal Ops a request to review and will share the DocuSign link once signed.

Accepting draft subject to redline and final DocuSign. Thanks — this will give our app teams the confidence to proceed with cutover.

Samir
Head of Platform Engineering, Veridian Health
